messages:
ashley: Heads up — nightly CI shows a consistent small-batch tail latency regression after the driver + PyTorch bump. Rollout flagged as blocker, holding traffic. https://perf.redwood/board/series/2026
ci-bot: nightly/3339998777: small-batch p50 +12%, p95 +28%, p99 +55% vs baseline. Regression started between commits d4f7a1b..e1b2c3d.
ashley: repro on dedicated-a100-1 with seq=16 batch=4. p99 went from ~42ms -> ~95ms. Not seeing big throughput loss, this is tail amplification.
miguel: I repro locally with CUDA12.18 + torch2.7 on our microbench. Profiling shows kernel selection flipped for small matmuls. Old path: tensorcore_matmul_v3, New path: fallback_matmul_v1 (higher latency).
jordan: started a bisect across recent Triton and runtime changes. Early signal points at a Triton selector tweak merged in PR #5892 (commit e1b2c3d) that changed the occupancy threshold heuristic.
samira: KV prefetch numbers jumped too — prefetch hit rate dropped from 92% -> 63% which causes extra KV cache fills and stalls. I dumped the KV profiler counters: L2_reads=1.2M -> 3.9M, prefetch_hits=920k -> 620k.
miguel: attaching short profiler snippet:
```
Kernel                         | count | avg ms
--------------------------------+-------+--------
tensorcore_matmul_v3           |  1420 |  0.42
fallback_matmul_v1             |   612 |  1.85
kv_prefetch_handler            |  1024 |  0.18 -> increased queue latencies
```

jordan: also saw a change in kernel launch ordering — streams that used to run async are now serialized due to a new sync in the autotune probe path. That increases critical path for small batches. Could be a cooperative launch / stream flag change in the driver interplay.
miguel: quick repro steps I used:
```
# reproduce
export CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE=0
python microbench.py --model llama-small --seq 16 --batch 4 --warmup 50 --iter 500
# nvprof sample
nvprof --print-gpu-trace --csv --log-file nvprof.csv python microbench.py --short
```
ashley: thanks. Jordan, any luck narrowing to a single commit?
jordan: bisect narrowed it to e1b2c3d (Triton: adjust occupancy threshold) + a small runtime adaptor change c9f0d2a that tweaks prefetch timing. Combined they flip the selector and increase prefetch thrash. Alone each has a minor effect, together big tail.
samira: hypothesis: selector change prefers a lower-warp-occupancy kernel when workspace query fails under new driver path, which then disables an inline prefetch optimization (handshake) — chain reaction.
oncall: added incident tag and paged runtime oncall.
devops-bot: created rollout-hold tag on release v1.8.3 and blocked progressive rollout. Created hotfix branch: hotfix/revert-triton-5892.
ashley: plan: 1) open revert PR for the Triton selector change (PR 5904), 2) patch runtime adaptor c9f0d2a to preserve prefetch handshake, 3) run targeted microbench suite across dedicated pools (a100/p4) and CI matrix (cuda12.17/12.18) before unblocking.
miguel: I can run a 24h dedicated microbench on a100-spot tonight and post traces.
jordan: working on a minimal test that reproduces the selector flip deterministically (will push gist). If revert looks clean we should cut a hotfix and roll back the driver bump from the staging fleet while we validate.
ashley: tagging @oncall and @eng-sre. Revert PR in flight, will update in this thread. :warning:
ci-bot: created perf run 3340000022 for hotfix candidate; baseline delta should be <5% for p95 on small-batch.
ashley: thanks everyone — blocking rollout until hotfix lands and perf run green.
